entry.summary: Svalbard needs no visa of its own. Every route goes through mainland Norway (Schengen), where Australians are visa-exempt for 90 days in 180. Svalbard is outside Schengen, so leaving it and returning counts as re-entry.
entry.next_check: Read the Governor of Svalbard's visitor rules (firearms and polar bear safety outside settlements, field travel notification).

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Leave no trace and don't pick flowers. Don't disturb birds or animals. It is illegal to lure, pursue or disturb polar bears: keep at least 300 m away (500 m from 1 March to 30 June) and retreat if one is close. Don't leave the settlements without suitable polar-bear protection and experience using it, or go with a guide. Loaded firearms are forbidden in Longyearbyen and in shops. Tourist landings outside settlements are only at mapped sites with a guide.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: Every trace of human activity from before 1946, plus graves, bones, whaling and walrus remains and old bear traps of any age, is automatically protected, with a 100 m zone around it. Don't touch, move or take anything.
culture-and-protocol.note: From the Norwegian state authority for Svalbard and the official visitor board.

laws.rule: Outside the settlements you must carry suitable means of scaring off polar bears; the Governor recommends a firearm. Polar bears are protected.
Non-resident visitors travelling in the field outside Management Area 10 must notify the Governor of Svalbard of their plans (tourism and field travel regulations).
Firearms can be temporarily imported or rented only with permission; applications can take up to 8 weeks.

items.text: Under section 2 of the Svalbard Act, Norwegian private and criminal law applies on Svalbard unless something else is set out. Norway's drug law therefore applies. Other Norwegian statutes apply only where stated.

public_holidays: Norway's public holidays apply on Svalbard (on Norway's record), including Constitution Day, 17 May (2027: Monday), which Longyearbyen marks with a children's parade.
moving_calendars: Svalbard's light cycle (signal, approximate): midnight sun from late April to late August; polar night from mid November to late January. The sun returns to Longyearbyen about 8 March, marked by the Sun Festival (Solfestuka).
